source_refs.note: Topic 2.5.1.1 Defining and Invoking Functions (PDF 46, printed 43). The call is printed greet('AH'); 'Ali' is meant. MCQ 8 is answered.

blocks.text: Functions are defined using the def keyword, followed by the function name and parentheses which may include parameters. The body of the function contains the code to be executed and must be indented.
def function_name (parameters): # code to be executed
Example: Define a function to greet a person.

def greet(name):
    print("As-Salaam-Alaikum", name)
    # Function invoking means call the function by name and perform the required task For example.
    greet (‘AH’)

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The call greet (‘AH’) is printed indented inside the function body, so it never runs and the program prints nothing. It must start at the left margin, after the function. The argument should be 'Ali' (as the explanation says) in straight quotes: greet('Ali').
Explanation: In this example, the greet function accepts a single parameter, name, with the value 'Ali'. It then prints a greeting message: 'As-Salaam-Alaikum  Ali'.
